dish: Handmade yellowtail fishball and pork-ball noodles, dry or soup
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-28/29, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand hawker across two adjoining stalls: noodle soup or 'dry' noodles with minced pork, pork balls or fish balls hand-made on the spot — the yellowtail fishballs are the draw.

dish: Handmade fishball noodles and mushroom minced-meat noodles (bak chor mee)
address: Holland Village Market & Food Centre, #01-14, 1 Lorong Mambong, Singapore 277700
w: A fishball-noodle lineage going back to a 1946 Chinatown pushcart: hand-made fishballs over springy mee pok ($4/$5) or a mushroom bak chor mee — the heritage bowl of Holland Village's food centre.

dish: Katong laksa (fragrant, coconut-dried-shrimp gravy) and nasi lemak
address: Holland Village Market & Food Centre, #01-15, 1 Lorong Mambong, Singapore 277700
w: A laksa that leans fragrant rather than fiery — prawns, fishcake, cockles and tau pok in a dried-shrimp-and-coconut gravy (premium $6.80) — beside a nasi lemak spread refined over decades.

dish: Economical fried bee hoon with sambal chicken wing, egg and vegetables
address: Holland Village Market & Food Centre, #01-11, 1 Lorong Mambong, Singapore 277700
w: The neighbourhood's breakfast stall: fried bee hoon or noodles from $1.20, topped with sambal chicken wing, egg and vegetables — sells out and shuts by early afternoon.

dish: Fried Hokkien prawn mee — white and yellow noodles in prawn-head, squid and pork-bone stock
n: Yuan Hokkien Fried Prawn Mee (Ghim Moh)
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)
w: A Margaret Drive Food Centre transplant: white and yellow noodles wok-fried down in a rich stock of prawn heads, squid and pork bones — one of the Ghim Moh picks shared by Women's Weekly and Her World.

dish: Thai stewed beef noodle soup with beef balls, slices and tendon
n: Yuan Authentic Thai Stewed Beef Noodle (Ghim Moh)
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)
w: Run by a cook from Chiang Rai: Thai stewed and sliced beef noodle soup — beefy, aromatic broth, beef balls, slices and tendon, small bowls from under $3 — a Thai hawker kitchen in an otherwise Chinese-heavy centre (Eatbook review; Women's Weekly and Her World Ghim Moh lists).

dish: Kway chap — flat rice sheets in herbal soy broth with braised offal, pork and egg
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-02, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: The kway chap stall Miss Tam Chiak calls chef Daniel Tay's favourite: silky rice sheets in a herbal braising broth with a spread of braised pork, offal and egg — written up by Daniel Food Diary, SG Food on Foot and in Eatbook's 13 best Holland Drive stalls.

dish: Nasi ayam penyet — smashed fried chicken with tempeh, tau kwa and sambal
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)
w: Holland Drive's Malay stall for ayam penyet: fragrant rice, fried chicken, tempeh, tau kwa, cucumber and sambal from about $4.50-$5 — on both Eatbook's and Women's Weekly's Holland Drive lists.

dish: Char siew and roast pork (sio bak) rice
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-36, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: The $3 char siew and roast pork rice that Eatbook headlines in its Holland Drive guide; Women's Weekly also lists it among the centre's 10 best.

dish: Fried carrot cake (chai tow kway), white or black
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044 (unit to confirm)
w: Black or white chai tow kway in $3/$4/$5 portions — the carrot cake pick of both Eatbook and Women's Weekly at Holland Drive.

dish: Shio pan (Japanese salted-butter rolls)
address: Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, #02-35, 44 Holland Drive, Singapore 270044
w: Young hawkers baking affordable shio pan from scratch inside a hawker centre — a newer Holland Drive draw named by Seth Lui's 11 best and covered by Eatbook.

dish: Warabimochi (bracken-starch mochi) and warabimochi drinks
address: 7 Holland Village Way, #01-54, One Holland Village, Singapore 275748
w: The Kamakura warabimochi specialist's Singapore flagship (Feb 2024): wobbly bracken-starch mochi and dessert drinks in coffee-milk, hojicha and strawberry-yoghurt flavours — still selling out a year on (Seth Lui); on Eatbook's and Honeycombers' Holland Village lists.

dish: Mexican restaurant classics
address: 32 Lorong Mambong, Holland Village, Singapore
w: One of Singapore's oldest Mexican restaurants, a Holland Village mainstay since 1990 — 'easy on the wallet and the stomach' (Seth Lui) and on Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village list.

dish: Lasagna, calzone and Venetian tiramisu
address: 26/26B Lorong Mambong, Holland Village, Singapore
w: A Holland Village Italian since 2006: lasagna, calzone, bruschetta and a traditional Venetian tiramisu — a constant on Lady Iron Chef's and Eatbook's Holland Village guides.

dish: Plated desserts by pastry chef Janice Wong
address: Lorong Liput, Holland Village, Singapore (unit to confirm at geocode)
w: Pastry chef Janice Wong's dessert bar — a Holland V institution that Honeycombers profiled through Wong's own neighbourhood picks, and on Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village list.

dish: Pancake stacks and all-day breakfast
address: One Holland Village, 7 Holland Village Way, Singapore 275748 (unit to confirm)
w: A Sydney-farmhouse-style grocer-café with an open charcoal grill, in-house dog bakery and ice-cream truck; the Signature Stack pancakes ($24) lead an all-day breakfast menu (Seth Lui; Eatbook).

dish: Crab cake Benedict and shakshuka brunch
address: Holland Village, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
w: Freshly ground coffee, bakes and a brunch menu led by a crab cake Benedict and shakshuka (Honeycombers) — also on Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village list.

dish: Roast duck, roast pork and char siew
address: Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre, 20 Ghim Moh Road, Singapore 270020 (unit to confirm)
w: A short-hours roast-meat counter (10am-2pm, Thursday to Sunday) for roast duck, crackling roast pork and char siew — reviewed by Miss Tam Chiak and listed by Women's Weekly / Her World among Ghim Moh's best.

dish: Vegetarian Mediterranean plates and vegetarian tandoori
address: Jalan Merah Saga, Chip Bee Gardens, Holland Village, Singapore (unit to confirm at geocode)
w: Chip Bee Gardens' long-standing vegetarian Mediterranean restaurant — meat-free plates including a vegetarian tandoori — on Lady Iron Chef's Chip Bee Gardens guide and Eatbook's current 25 best Holland Village list.

dish: Belgian waffles with soft-serve
address: Jalan Merah Saga, Chip Bee Gardens, Holland Village, Singapore (unit to confirm at geocode)
w: The Chip Bee Gardens dessert café famous for its Belgian waffles — in Lady Iron Chef's Chip Bee Gardens guide and The Ordinary Patrons' Chip Bee cafés round-up (2022).

dish: Pizza
address: Holland Village, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
w: A Holland Village pizza stop named by both Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village places and HungryGoWhere's 15 Holland Village restaurants.

dish: British-Indian curry-house curries
address: Holland Village, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
w: A British-style Indian curry house in Holland V, on Eatbook's and HungryGoWhere's Holland Village lists.

dish: Korean charcoal barbecue
n: Wang Dae Bak Korean BBQ (Holland Village)
address: Holland Village, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
w: Korean barbecue grilled at the table — on Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village list and HungryGoWhere's 15 Holland Village restaurants.

dish: Korean street food — tteokbokki, sausage gimbap, kimchi pancake, oden soup
address: 26A Lorong Mambong, Holland Village, Singapore 277685
w: A casual pojangmacha-style Korean bar-eatery with a street-food menu of tteokbokki, sausage gimbap, kimchi pancake, oden soup and ramyeon (Honeycombers); also on HungryGoWhere's Holland Village list.

dish: Modern Japanese
address: Holland Village, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
w: A modern Japanese restaurant in Holland V, on Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village places and HungryGoWhere's 15 Holland Village restaurants.

dish: Hong Kong egg tarts and cha chaan teng fare
address: Holland Village, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
w: The Hong Kong egg-tart bakery's Holland Village shop, home to its only cha chaan teng (Hong Kong-style tea house) in Singapore (Seth Lui); on Eatbook's 25 best Holland Village list.
